note: Diagnostic for the direct fix the routed-writes measurement pointed to: ordinary note writes refresh only the paths they wrote.
commit: the commit that adds this file, against 21d1aaee
binary: target/release/vulcan (cargo build --release -p vulcan-cli) for both commits
fixtures: mdb-100k/collection: scripts/generate_mdb_fixture.py (generator v1, seed 42, 100,000 records), scanned with `scan --full`

machine.host: development laptop, not the designated evaluation host (Intel Core i7-8650U, 31 GiB RAM, Debian 13)

setup: Isolated XDG_CONFIG_HOME, XDG_STATE_HOME, XDG_DATA_HOME, and XDG_CACHE_HOME; no daemon; stdin closed

method.timing: wall clock from Python; 9 runs per case, the first discarded; p50 of 8

findings: Every ordinary note write refreshed the cache with a full incremental scan, which discovers every file in the vault even when one note changed. Refreshing only the written paths (vulcan_core::scan::scan_vault_paths_unlocked) makes a write at 100K notes about 6.5 times faster.

In an mdbase collection the remaining time is mdbase's managed-write check: build_mdbase_write_preview calls discover_record_stats, which walks every file to validate the collection on each write (1,382 directories at 100K records). That is a separate mdbase fix.
